cancel_deployment.description: Stop a deployment that is still queued or building. One that has already finished can't be canceled.
cancel_deployment.name: cancel_deployment

parameters.description: The deployment's id (starts with 'dpl_'), as List deployments or the Deployment finished trigger gives it, or its address, such as my-app-abc123.vercel.app.

parameters.description: Optional Vercel Team id or slug to act on behalf of a team. Leave empty to use the personal account the access token belongs to.

create_environment_variable.description: Add an environment variable to a project so its deployments can read it: an API key, a feature flag, a service URL, and so on.
create_environment_variable.name: create_environment_variable

parameters.description: The project's id (starts with 'prj_') or its name. Use the id returned by Create a project, or a value from List projects.
parameters.name: project_id

parameters.description: The environment variable name, for example 'API_URL'.
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: The environment variable value.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: Which environments the variable applies to. Defaults to all of production, preview, and development when left empty.
parameters.name: target

parameters.description: How Vercel stores the value: 'encrypted' (default, a standard secret), 'plain' (readable in the dashboard), or 'sensitive' (write-only, never shown again).
parameters.name: type

parameters.description: Optional git branch to scope the variable to (for the preview target).
parameters.name: git_branch

parameters.description: Optional note describing what the variable is for.
parameters.name: comment

parameters.description: When on, update the value of an existing variable with the same key/target instead of failing on a conflict.
parameters.name: upsert

parameters.description: Optional Vercel Team id or slug to act on behalf of a team. Leave empty to use the personal account the access token belongs to.
parameters.name: team_id

created.description: The created variable, with fields such as id, key, target, type, and createdAt (the value is not returned for encrypted/sensitive types).

failed.description: Any variables Vercel rejected, with an error explaining why (empty on success).

create_project.description: Create a new Vercel project by name and get back its id. A framework preset is optional; Vercel auto-detects one on the first deployment when omitted.
create_project.name: create_project

parameters.description: The new project's name: lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', up to 100 characters (for example 'my-app'). Must be unique within the account.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: Optional framework preset slug. Leave empty to let Vercel auto-detect.
parameters.name: framework

parameters.description: Optional Vercel Team id or slug to act on behalf of a team. Leave empty to use the personal account the access token belongs to.
parameters.name: team_id

accountId.description: The owning account (personal or team) id.

framework.description: The detected or supplied framework preset, or null if none.

id.description: The new project's id (starts with 'prj_'); use it as Project ID in other actions.

redeploy.description: Build a deployment again as a new deployment. By default it goes to the same environment: a production deployment to production, a preview to preview. It uses the same commit unless you ask for the branch's latest one. Returns the new deployment, which starts building straight away.
redeploy.name: redeploy

parameters.description: The deployment's id (starts with 'dpl_'), as List deployments or the Deployment finished trigger gives it, or its address, such as my-app-abc123.vercel.app.
parameters.name: deployment_id

parameters.description: Where the new deployment goes. Leave it on the same environment as the original to redeploy as the dashboard does.
parameters.name: target

options.label: The same environment as the original

parameters.description: Build the newest commit on the deployment's branch instead of the same commit again.
parameters.name: use_latest_commit

parameters.description: Optional Vercel Team id or slug to act on behalf of a team. Leave empty to use the personal account the access token belongs to.

description: Manage your Vercel projects, deployments, and environment variables: list projects and deployments, look up, redeploy, cancel or delete a deployment, create projects, set environment variables, delete projects, and start a workflow when a deployment finishes.

vercel_deployment_finished_trigger.description: Runs when a Vercel deployment finishes: it is ready, it failed or it was canceled, with its address, environment, branch and commit, and why it failed if it did. Deployments that had finished when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.branch: The Git branch it was built from.
output.created: When it was created, in milliseconds since 1970.
output.creator: Who started it (their username).
output.error_message: Why it failed or was canceled, if it was.
output.inspector_url: Its page in the Vercel dashboard, with the build logs.
output.name: The project's name.
output.outcome: The same in words: ready, failed or canceled.
output.ready: When it became ready, in milliseconds since 1970.
output.target: Where it was deployed: production, staging or preview.
